2PC.name: Two-Phase Commit
2PC.def: A protocol that makes several participants all commit a transaction or all abort it: prepare, then commit.

ABAC.name: Attribute-Based Access Control
ABAC.def: Authorization decided by rules over attributes of the user, resource and context.

ACID.name: Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, Durability
ACID.def: A set of properties of database transactions intended to guarantee data validity despite errors.

AI.name: Artificial Intelligence
AI.def: Software that performs tasks that normally need human judgment, such as understanding language or recognising images.

ALU.name: Arithmetic Logic Unit
ALU.def: The circuit in a CPU core that performs integer arithmetic, comparisons and bitwise operations.

ANS.name: Asymmetric Numeral Systems
ANS.def: An entropy-coding method that approaches the Shannon limit with fractional bits per symbol; used in zstd.

API.name: Application Programming Interface
API.def: A contract that lets one program call another: the operations, inputs, outputs and errors it promises.

AST.name: Abstract Syntax Tree
AST.def: A tree representation of the abstract syntactic structure of source code written in a programming language.

AUC.name: Area Under the ROC Curve
AUC.def: The chance a model scores a random positive example above a random negative one; 0.5 is guessing, 1.0 is perfect.

AVL.name: Adelson-Velsky and Landis Tree
AVL.def: A self-balancing binary search tree where the heights of the two child subtrees of any node differ by at most one.

AVX.name: Advanced Vector Extensions
AVX.def: x86 SIMD instructions that operate on 256- or 512-bit registers holding several values at once.

BASE.name: Basically Available, Soft state, Eventual consistency
BASE.def: A consistency model used by many NoSQL databases, prioritizing availability over strict consistency.

BDP.name: Bandwidth-Delay Product
BDP.def: Bandwidth × round-trip time: how much data must be in flight, unacknowledged, to keep a network path fully busy.

BFS.name: Breadth-First Search
BFS.def: An algorithm for traversing or searching tree or graph data structures level by level.

BPE.name: Byte Pair Encoding
BPE.def: A tokenizer that starts from bytes and repeatedly merges the most frequent adjacent pair into a new token.

BST.name: Binary Search Tree
BST.def: A node-based binary tree data structure where the left subtree has smaller values and the right subtree has larger values than the parent node.

CAP.name: CAP theorem
CAP.def: When a network partition splits a distributed store, it must choose between Consistency (every read sees the latest write) and Availability (every request gets an answer). Without a partition you can have both.

CAS.name: Compare-And-Swap
CAS.def: An atomic instruction used in multithreading to achieve synchronization by comparing and potentially modifying a memory location.

CD.name: Continuous Delivery / Deployment
CD.def: Every change that passes the pipeline is releasable (delivery) or released automatically (deployment).

CDC.name: Change Data Capture
CDC.def: Streaming a database's committed changes out of its log so other systems can react to them.

CDN.name: Content Delivery Network
CDN.def: A geographically distributed network of proxy servers and their data centers used to deliver content with low latency.

CFS.name: Completely Fair Scheduler
CFS.def: The Linux process scheduler from 2.6.23 to 6.5: it runs the task with the least virtual runtime. Linux 6.6 replaced it with EEVDF.

CI.name: Continuous Integration
CI.def: The practice of merging all developers' working copies to a shared mainline several times a day.

CI/CD.name: Continuous Integration / Continuous Delivery
CI/CD.def: Every change is built and tested automatically (CI) and kept releasable, or released, through an automated pipeline (CD).

CLI.name: Command-Line Interface
CLI.def: A text interface where you type commands, such as a shell or a tool like git or kubectl.

CLT.name: Central Limit Theorem
CLT.def: The average of many independent samples is approximately normally distributed, with spread σ/√n.

CMOV.name: Conditional Move
CMOV.def: An x86 instruction that copies a value only if a condition holds, letting compilers remove a branch.

CNN.name: Convolutional Neural Network
CNN.def: A neural network that slides small learned filters over its input; the classic architecture for images.

CPU.name: Central Processing Unit
CPU.def: The primary component of a computer that acts as its 'brain', executing instructions of a computer program.

CRC.name: Cyclic Redundancy Check
CRC.def: An error-detecting code computed as a polynomial remainder over bits; catches burst errors, not tampering.

CRDT.name: Conflict-free Replicated Data Type
CRDT.def: A data structure whose replicas can be updated independently and always merge to the same state without coordination.

CRT.name: Chinese Remainder Theorem
CRT.def: Remainders modulo pairwise coprime numbers determine a number uniquely modulo their product.

CRUD.name: Create, Read, Update, Delete
CRUD.def: The four basic functions of persistent storage operations, commonly used in database and API design.

CSP.name: Content Security Policy
CSP.def: A browser header listing which scripts and resources a page may load, blocking most injected scripts.

CSRF.name: Cross-Site Request Forgery
CSRF.def: An attack that makes a logged-in user's browser send an unwanted request to a site that trusts its cookies.

DAG.name: Directed Acyclic Graph
DAG.def: A directed graph with no directed cycles, consisting of vertices and edges where each edge is directed from one vertex to another.

DAU.name: Daily Active Users
DAU.def: Distinct users who use a product on a given day; the usual starting number for capacity estimates.

DDL.name: Data Definition Language
DDL.def: Syntax for creating and modifying database objects such as tables, indices, and users.

DFA.name: Deterministic Finite Automaton
DFA.def: A machine with finitely many states and exactly one transition per state and input symbol; recognises regular languages.

DFS.name: Depth-First Search
DFS.def: An algorithm for traversing or searching tree or graph data structures by exploring as far as possible along each branch before backtracking.

DLQ.name: Dead-Letter Queue
DLQ.def: Where messages go after repeated processing failures, so they stop blocking the rest and can be inspected and replayed.

DMA.name: Direct Memory Access
DMA.def: A device copying data to or from RAM without the CPU moving each byte.

DNS.name: Domain Name System
DNS.def: A hierarchical and decentralized naming system for computers, services, or other resources connected to the Internet.

DP.name: Dynamic Programming
DP.def: A method for solving complex problems by breaking them down into simpler overlapping subproblems and storing the results.

DPO.name: Direct Preference Optimization
DPO.def: Aligns a model on pairs of preferred and rejected answers directly, without training a separate reward model as RLHF does.

DRY.name: Don't Repeat Yourself
DRY.def: A software development principle aimed at reducing repetition of software patterns, replacing it with abstractions.

DVC.name: Data Version Control
DVC.def: A tool that versions datasets and models alongside Git, storing the large files in remote storage.

ECC.name: Error-Correcting Code
ECC.def: Redundant encoding that lets a receiver detect and repair corrupted bits; also memory that uses one.

EEVDF.name: Earliest Eligible Virtual Deadline First
EEVDF.def: The Linux fair scheduler since kernel 6.6: it keeps CFS's virtual-runtime accounting and runs the eligible task with the earliest virtual deadline.

EOF.name: End of File
EOF.def: The signal that no more data will arrive; on a socket, a read returning zero bytes because the other side closed the connection.

EWMA.name: Exponentially Weighted Moving Average
EWMA.def: A running average in which older samples' weights decay exponentially.

FCFS.name: First Come, First Served
FCFS.def: A scheduling policy that runs work in arrival order, each item to completion.

FIFO.name: First-In, First-Out
FIFO.def: A method for processing data where the first items entered are the first to be removed, characteristic of queue data structures.

FLP.name: Fischer, Lynch and Paterson
FLP.def: The 1985 result that no deterministic consensus algorithm can guarantee termination in an asynchronous system if one node may crash.

GAN.name: Generative Adversarial Network
GAN.def: Two networks trained against each other: a generator makes fake samples and a discriminator tries to tell them from real ones.

GC.name: Garbage Collection
GC.def: A form of automatic memory management that attempts to reclaim garbage, or memory occupied by objects that are no longer in use by the program.

GIL.name: Global Interpreter Lock
GIL.def: A mutex that protects access to Python objects, preventing multiple threads from executing Python bytecodes at once.

GPU.name: Graphics Processing Unit
GPU.def: A processor with thousands of simple cores and very fast memory, used to train and serve machine-learning models.

gRPC.name: gRPC Remote Procedure Call
gRPC.def: A modern, open-source, high-performance RPC framework that can run in any environment.

GRU.name: Gated Recurrent Unit
GRU.def: A recurrent cell with update and reset gates; a simpler alternative to the LSTM.

GUI.name: Graphical User Interface
GUI.def: A form of user interface that allows users to interact with electronic devices through graphical icons.

HDD.name: Hard Disk Drive
HDD.def: An electro-mechanical data storage device that stores and retrieves digital data using magnetic storage.

HLC.name: Hybrid Logical Clock
HLC.def: A timestamp of physical time plus a logical counter: respects causality and stays close to wall-clock time.

HMAC.name: Hash-based Message Authentication Code
HMAC.def: A keyed hash that proves a message was produced by someone holding the secret key and was not changed.

HNSW.name: Hierarchical Navigable Small World
HNSW.def: A graph-based approximate nearest-neighbour index that searches greedily from coarse to fine layers.

HSM.name: Hardware Security Module
HSM.def: Tamper-resistant hardware that stores keys and performs cryptographic operations inside it.

HSTS.name: HTTP Strict Transport Security
HSTS.def: A header telling browsers to use only HTTPS for a site, preventing downgrade to plain HTTP.

HTTP.name: Hypertext Transfer Protocol
HTTP.def: The foundation of data communication for the World Wide Web, operating on a client-server model.

HTTPS.name: Hypertext Transfer Protocol Secure
HTTPS.def: An extension of HTTP that uses encryption for secure communication over a computer network.

IDE.name: Integrated Development Environment
IDE.def: A software application that provides comprehensive facilities to computer programmers for software development.

IDOR.name: Insecure Direct Object Reference
IDOR.def: An access-control bug where changing an ID in a request returns someone else's data because ownership is not checked.

IEEE.name: Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers
IEEE.def: Standards body; IEEE 754 is the floating-point format every mainstream CPU implements.

ILP.name: Instruction-Level Parallelism · Integer Linear Programming
ILP.def: Instruction-Level Parallelism: A CPU core executing several independent instructions at the same time. Integer Linear Programming: Optimising a linear objective under linear constraints with integer variables; NP-hard but well served by solvers.

IP.name: Internet Protocol
IP.def: The principal communications protocol in the Internet protocol suite for relaying datagrams across network boundaries.

IPC.name: Inter-Process Communication
IPC.def: Mechanisms for separate processes to exchange data: pipes, sockets, shared memory, message queues.

ISA.name: Instruction Set Architecture
ISA.def: The set of machine instructions a CPU understands, such as x86-64 or ARM64.

IVF.name: Inverted File index
IVF.def: An approximate nearest-neighbour index that clusters vectors and searches only the clusters nearest the query.

JSON.name: JavaScript Object Notation
JSON.def: A lightweight data-interchange format that is easy for humans to read/write and machines to parse/generate.

JVM.name: Java Virtual Machine
JVM.def: An abstract computing machine that enables a computer to run a Java program.

JWT.name: JSON Web Token
JWT.def: A compact, URL-safe means of representing claims to be transferred between two parties, often used for authentication.

K8s.name: Kubernetes
K8s.def: An open-source system that schedules containers onto a cluster of machines and keeps them running at the declared state.

KISS.name: Keep It Simple, Stupid
KISS.def: A design principle noting that most systems work best if they are kept simple rather than made complicated.

KMP.name: Knuth-Morris-Pratt
KMP.def: A string-searching algorithm that searches for occurrences of a word within a main text string in optimal time.

KMS.name: Key Management Service
KMS.def: A managed service that stores encryption keys and performs operations with them, so keys never leave it.

LB.name: Load Balancer
LB.def: A device or software service that distributes network or application traffic across a number of servers to improve capacity and reliability.

LCA.name: Lowest Common Ancestor
LCA.def: In a tree or directed acyclic graph, the lowest node that has both given nodes as descendants.

LCP.name: Longest Common Prefix
LCP.def: The shared prefix of maximum length among a set of strings.

LCS.name: Longest Common Subsequence
LCS.def: The problem of finding the longest subsequence common to all sequences in a set of sequences.

LFU.name: Least Frequently Used
LFU.def: A cache replacement policy that discards the least frequently used items first.

LIFO.name: Last-In, First-Out
LIFO.def: A method for processing data where the last items entered are the first to be removed, characteristic of stack data structures.

LIS.name: Longest Increasing Subsequence
LIS.def: The problem of finding a subsequence of a given sequence in which the elements are in sorted order.

LLM.name: Large Language Model
LLM.def: A neural network (usually a Transformer) trained on huge amounts of text to predict the next token.

LoRA.name: Low-Rank Adaptation
LoRA.def: Fine-tuning that freezes the model and trains small low-rank matrices added to chosen weight layers.

LP.name: Linear Programming
LP.def: Optimising a linear objective under linear constraints over real numbers; solvable in polynomial time.

LRU.name: Least Recently Used
LRU.def: A cache replacement policy that discards the least recently used items first when the cache reaches its capacity.

LSM.name: Log-Structured Merge-tree
LSM.def: A data structure with performance characteristics that make it attractive for providing indexed access to files with high insert volume.

LSTM.name: Long Short-Term Memory
LSTM.def: A recurrent cell whose gates control what to keep, forget and output, so it can learn longer dependencies than a plain RNN.

LWW.name: Last Writer Wins
LWW.def: A conflict rule that keeps the write with the latest timestamp and silently discards the others.

LZ77.name: Lempel–Ziv 1977
LZ77.def: Compression by replacing repeated substrings with back-references; the first stage of DEFLATE (gzip, zip, PNG).

MCMC.name: Markov Chain Monte Carlo
MCMC.def: Sampling from a hard-to-compute distribution by running a random walk whose long-run distribution is the target.

MCP.name: Model Context Protocol
MCP.def: An open protocol that lets an AI application discover and call tools, resources and prompts exposed by servers.

MESI.name: Modified, Exclusive, Shared, Invalid
MESI.def: The cache-coherence protocol states that keep each core's cached copy of a line consistent.

MIME.name: Multipurpose Internet Mail Extensions
MIME.def: The type labels, such as image/png, that say what kind of content a file or HTTP body claims to be.

ML.name: Machine Learning
ML.def: Building systems that learn patterns from data instead of following hand-written rules.

MMU.name: Memory Management Unit
MMU.def: The CPU hardware that translates virtual addresses to physical ones using page tables and the TLB.

MoE.name: Mixture of Experts
MoE.def: A layer with many expert sub-networks where a router sends each token to only a few of them, so parameters grow faster than compute.

MRO.name: Method Resolution Order
MRO.def: The order in which a programming language resolves a method or attribute in a class hierarchy.

MST.name: Minimum Spanning Tree
MST.def: A subset of the edges of a connected, edge-weighted undirected graph that connects all vertices with the minimum possible total edge weight.

MVCC.name: Multi-Version Concurrency Control
MVCC.def: The database keeps several versions of a row so readers see a consistent snapshot and do not block writers (and writers do not block readers).

NaN.name: Not a Number
NaN.def: The floating-point value produced by undefined operations such as 0/0; it is not equal to anything, itself included.

NFA.name: Nondeterministic Finite Automaton
NFA.def: A finite automaton that may be in several states at once; equivalent in power to a DFA.

NLP.name: Natural Language Processing
NLP.def: Computing with human language: classification, translation, extraction, generation.

NoSQL.name: Not Only SQL
NoSQL.def: A broad class of database management systems that differ from the classic relational model, designed for distributed data stores.

NTP.name: Network Time Protocol
NTP.def: The protocol that synchronises machine clocks against reference servers, typically to within milliseconds.

NUMA.name: Non-Uniform Memory Access
NUMA.def: A multi-socket design where each CPU has local memory that is faster to reach than another CPU's memory.

OAEP.name: Optimal Asymmetric Encryption Padding
OAEP.def: Randomised padding that makes RSA encryption secure against attacks on textbook RSA.

OCC.name: Optimistic Concurrency Control
OCC.def: Letting transactions run without locks and checking for conflicts at commit, aborting one if they conflict.

OIDC.name: OpenID Connect
OIDC.def: An identity layer on top of OAuth 2.0: an ID token tells the app who the user is.

OLAP.name: Online Analytical Processing
OLAP.def: Workloads that scan and aggregate large amounts of data, usually on column-oriented storage.

OLTP.name: Online Transaction Processing
OLTP.def: Workloads of many small reads and writes by key, such as placing orders, usually on row-oriented storage.

OOM.name: Out of Memory
OOM.def: An undesired state of computer operation where no additional memory can be allocated for use by programs.

OOP.name: Object-Oriented Programming
OOP.def: A programming paradigm based on the concept of 'objects', which can contain data and code.

ORM.name: Object-Relational Mapping
ORM.def: A programming technique for converting data between incompatible type systems using object-oriented programming languages.

OS.name: Operating System
OS.def: System software that manages computer hardware, software resources, and provides common services for computer programs.

PACELC.name: Partition: Availability or Consistency; Else: Latency or Consistency
PACELC.def: An extension of CAP: during a partition choose A or C, and otherwise choose between low latency and consistency.

PCA.name: Principal Component Analysis
PCA.def: Finds the orthogonal directions of greatest variance in data, used for dimensionality reduction.

PEFT.name: Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning
PEFT.def: Fine-tuning methods (LoRA, adapters, prefix tuning) that train a small fraction of the parameters.

PEP.name: Python Enhancement Proposal
PEP.def: A design document providing information to the Python community, describing a new feature or its environment.

PID.name: Process Identifier
PID.def: The number the kernel assigns to each process.

PII.name: Personally Identifiable Information
PII.def: Data that can identify a person, such as a name, email address or location, and needs extra protection.

PKCE.name: Proof Key for Code Exchange
PKCE.def: An OAuth extension: the client proves, with a secret verifier, that it started the flow, so an intercepted authorization code is useless.

QLoRA.name: Quantized Low-Rank Adaptation
QLoRA.def: LoRA training on top of a base model quantized to 4 bits, so large models fit on one GPU.

QPS.name: Queries Per Second
QPS.def: A common metric used to measure the rate of traffic passing through a particular server or system.

QUIC.name: QUIC
QUIC.def: A transport protocol over UDP with built-in TLS 1.3 and independent streams; HTTP/3 runs on it.

RAG.name: Retrieval-Augmented Generation
RAG.def: Retrieve relevant documents first, then give them to the LLM in the prompt so the answer is grounded in them.

RAID.name: Redundant Array of Independent Disks
RAID.def: Combines disks for redundancy and/or speed; RAID-5 stores XOR parity to rebuild one failed disk.

RAII.name: Resource Acquisition Is Initialization
RAII.def: Tying a resource's lifetime to an object's scope, so leaving the scope releases it (C++, Rust).

RAM.name: Random Access Memory
RAM.def: A form of computer memory that can be read and changed in any order, typically used to store working data.

RBAC.name: Role-Based Access Control
RBAC.def: Authorization by assigning permissions to roles and roles to users.

RE2.name: RE2 regular expression engine
RE2.def: Google's automaton-based regex library that guarantees linear-time matching (no backreferences).

ReBAC.name: Relationship-Based Access Control
ReBAC.def: Authorization derived from relationships between users and objects, as in Google's Zanzibar.

ReDoS.name: Regular expression Denial of Service
ReDoS.def: An attack that sends input causing a backtracking regex engine to take exponential time.

REST.name: Representational State Transfer
REST.def: An architectural style for distributed hypermedia systems, commonly used for creating interactive web services.

RFO.name: Read For Ownership
RFO.def: The cache-coherence request a core sends to get exclusive ownership of a cache line before writing it, invalidating other cores' copies.

RLHF.name: Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback
RLHF.def: Train a reward model on human preference rankings, then optimise the LLM against it (often with PPO).

RNN.name: Recurrent Neural Network
RNN.def: A network that processes a sequence one step at a time, carrying a hidden state forward.

RPC.name: Remote Procedure Call
RPC.def: A protocol that allows one program to request a service from a program located in another computer on a network.

RPO.name: Recovery Point Objective
RPO.def: How much data you can afford to lose in a failure, measured as time: the window of writes that may be gone.

RSA.name: Rivest–Shamir–Adleman
RSA.def: Public-key cryptosystem whose security rests on the difficulty of factoring the product of two large primes.

RSS.name: Resident Set Size
RSS.def: The physical memory a process currently occupies.

RST.name: TCP Reset
RST.def: A TCP segment that aborts a connection immediately; a client sees it as connection refused or connection reset.

RTO.name: Recovery Time Objective
RTO.def: How long a service may be down after a failure before it must be back.

RTT.name: Round-Trip Time
RTT.def: The time for a packet to reach the other end and a reply to come back.

SaaS.name: Software as a Service
SaaS.def: A software licensing and delivery model in which software is licensed on a subscription basis and is centrally hosted.

SAT.name: Boolean satisfiability
SAT.def: Is there an assignment making a Boolean formula true? The first problem proved NP-complete.

SDK.name: Software Development Kit
SDK.def: A collection of software development tools in one installable package.

SECDED.name: Single Error Correction, Double Error Detection
SECDED.def: An extended Hamming code used in ECC memory: fixes one flipped bit, detects two.

SGD.name: Stochastic Gradient Descent
SGD.def: Update the weights with the gradient computed on a small random batch instead of the whole dataset.

SIMD.name: Single Instruction, Multiple Data
SIMD.def: One instruction operating on several values packed into a wide register.

SJF.name: Shortest Job First
SJF.def: A scheduling policy that runs the job with the shortest expected run time next, minimising average waiting time.

SLA.name: Service Level Agreement
SLA.def: A commitment between a service provider and a client outlining expected performance metrics such as availability.

SLI.name: Service Level Indicator
SLI.def: A carefully defined quantitative measure of some aspect of the level of service that is provided, such as latency.

SLO.name: Service Level Objective
SLO.def: A specific target level for the reliability of a service, usually defined by a numerical goal for a metric.

SMT.name: Simultaneous Multithreading · Satisfiability Modulo Theories
SMT.def: Simultaneous Multithreading: Running two hardware threads on one core's execution units (Intel calls it Hyper-Threading). Satisfiability Modulo Theories: SAT extended with theories such as integers and arrays; used in program verification and solvers.

SNI.name: Server Name Indication
SNI.def: A TLS field in which the client names the site it wants, so one IP address can serve many certificates.

SOAP.name: Simple Object Access Protocol
SOAP.def: A messaging protocol specification for exchanging structured information in the implementation of web services.

SOLID.name: SOLID principles
SOLID.def: Five object-oriented design principles: Single responsibility, Open–closed, Liskov substitution, Interface segregation, Dependency inversion.

SPIFFE.name: Secure Production Identity Framework for Everyone
SPIFFE.def: A standard for giving workloads cryptographic identities (SPIFFE IDs and SVIDs) instead of shared secrets.

SQL.name: Structured Query Language
SQL.def: A standard language for storing, manipulating and retrieving data in databases.

SRTF.name: Shortest Remaining Time First
SRTF.def: The preemptive version of shortest job first: a newly arrived shorter job interrupts the running one.

SSD.name: Solid-State Drive
SSD.def: A solid-state storage device that uses integrated circuit assemblies to store data persistently, offering faster access times.

SSE.name: Server-Sent Events
SSE.def: A standard describing how servers can initiate data transmission towards clients once an initial connection is established.

SSI.name: Serializable Snapshot Isolation
SSI.def: PostgreSQL's serializable level: snapshot isolation plus tracking of read/write dependencies, aborting a transaction when the interleaving could not have happened one at a time.

SSL.name: Secure Sockets Layer
SSL.def: The predecessor to TLS, a cryptographic protocol providing communications security over a network.

SSRF.name: Server-Side Request Forgery
SSRF.def: An attack that makes a server fetch a URL of the attacker's choosing, often reaching internal services.

STW.name: Stop-The-World
STW.def: A garbage-collection pause during which all program threads are halted.

SVD.name: Singular Value Decomposition
SVD.def: Factoring a matrix as U·Σ·Vᵀ; the largest singular values give the best low-rank approximation.

SWIM.name: Scalable Weakly-consistent Infection-style Membership
SWIM.def: A gossip-based protocol for cluster membership and failure detection, used by Consul and memberlist.

TCO.name: Tail Call Optimization
TCO.def: Reusing the current stack frame for a call in tail position, so deep tail recursion uses constant stack. Python and Go do not do it.

TCP.name: Transmission Control Protocol
TCP.def: A core protocol of the Internet Protocol Suite that provides reliable, ordered, and error-checked delivery of a stream of bytes.

TDD.name: Test-Driven Development
TDD.def: A software development process relying on software requirements being converted to test cases before software is fully developed.

TLB.name: Translation Lookaside Buffer
TLB.def: A memory cache that stores recent translations of virtual memory to physical addresses for faster retrieval.

TLS.name: Transport Layer Security
TLS.def: A cryptographic protocol designed to provide communications security over a computer network.

TOCTOU.name: Time Of Check To Time Of Use
TOCTOU.def: A race where a condition checked earlier is no longer true when acted on.

TSP.name: Travelling Salesman Problem
TSP.def: Find the shortest tour visiting every city once; NP-hard.

TTFT.name: Time To First Token
TTFT.def: How long an LLM takes to produce the first token of its response; what users perceive as responsiveness.

TTL.name: Time To Live
TTL.def: How long a cached value, DNS record or packet stays valid before it expires.

UDP.name: User Datagram Protocol
UDP.def: A simple, connectionless communication protocol that allows for sending messages with minimal overhead but no delivery guarantees.

ULID.name: Universally Unique Lexicographically Sortable Identifier
ULID.def: A 128-bit ID that starts with a millisecond timestamp, so IDs sort roughly by creation time.

ULP.name: Unit in the Last Place
ULP.def: The gap between a floating-point number and the next representable one.

UTF.name: Unicode Transformation Format
UTF.def: A family of character encodings capable of encoding all possible Unicode code points.

UUID.name: Universally Unique Identifier
UUID.def: A 128-bit label used for information in computer systems to ensure uniqueness across distributed systems.

vDSO.name: virtual Dynamic Shared Object
vDSO.def: A small library the kernel maps into every process so calls like clock_gettime run without entering the kernel.

VM.name: Virtual Machine
VM.def: The virtualization/emulation of a computer system.

WAL.name: Write-Ahead Logging
WAL.def: A family of techniques for providing atomicity and durability in database systems by writing modifications to a log before they are applied.

XML.name: Extensible Markup Language
XML.def: A markup language that defines a set of rules for encoding documents in a format that is both human-readable and machine-readable.

XOR.name: Exclusive OR
XOR.def: A bitwise operation that evaluates to true if and only if its arguments differ.

XSS.name: Cross-Site Scripting
XSS.def: An attack that injects script into a page other users view, so it runs with their session.

YAGNI.name: You Aren't Gonna Need It
YAGNI.def: A principle of extreme programming that states a programmer should not add functionality until deemed necessary.
